scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC users report no noticeable problems with internal traffic.
Internet access also works. But network monitoring shows R1's
ECMP path count dropped from 2 to 1 and all internet traffic
now takes a single path through CSW2 only. CSW1 reports an
OSPF neighbor went down. What changed?

injection.action: shut down the link to r1

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: csw1 eth0 / link CSW1 <-> R1 (10.0.0.32/30)
Mechanism: r1 has two ECMP-eligible paths to the OSPF backbone
  via CSW1 (10.0.0.33) and CSW2 (10.0.0.37). With CSW1's eth0
  down, the adjacency drops and the CSW1-side path is removed.
  All traffic falls onto the CSW2 path; capacity is halved
  but no outage because OSPF converges.
Localization: csw1 (eth0)
Root cause: physical/logical link between CSW1 and R1 is down
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` on csw1 (or investigate cabling if
  in real hardware)
scenario.fix_spec:

agent.diagnosis_text:
Subsystem affected: Layer1/Interface state causing OSPF adjacency loss. Mechanism: R1 previously had two equal-cost OSPF paths into the campus core via CSW1 (r1.eth0–csw1.eth0) and CSW2 (r1.eth1–csw2.eth0). With CSW1’s WAN-facing link down, its OSPF adjacency to R1 dropped; R1 now only learns internal routes via CSW2, so ECMP shrank from 2 to 1 and all traffic takes the CSW2 path.

Localization and evidence:
- On CSW1, the WAN port is down: ethtool eth0 shows “Link detected: no” and ip addr reports eth0 state DOWN with 10.0.0.34/30 (CD_WAN_LINK_1). CSW1’s OSPF neighbors do not include R1 (10.0.0.76).
- On R1, OSPF-learned routes are installed only via 10.0.0.38 (eth1 toward CSW2); there are no multipath entries via 10.0.0.34 (eth0 toward CSW1).
- R1 still has Internet via ISP on eth2, and intra-campus reachability remains normal via CSW2, matching the user report.

Root cause: The CSW1-to-R1 link (csw1.eth0 on CD_WAN_LINK_1) is down/administratively disabled, removing the OSPF adjacency and eliminating one ECMP path.

Corrective fix: Restore CSW1’s eth0 on CD_WAN_LINK_1 (verify cabling/veth, “ip link set dev eth0 up” if administratively down). OSPF is already configured for 10.0.0.32/30 on CSW1; once the link comes up, the R1–CSW1 neighbor will reestablish and ECMP (2 paths) will return. Monitor OSPF neighbors on CSW1/R1 to confirm stability.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names the CSW1–R1 link (csw1.eth0 <-> r1.eth0 / CD_WAN_LINK_1) as down and ties OSPF adjacency loss to that interface.
The report explicitly identifies csw1.eth0 as down (link state DOWN/Link detected: no) and ties the OSPF adjacency loss to that interface.
The report explicitly identifies two ECMP OSPF paths via CSW1 and CSW2 and explains that CSW1’s link failure reduced ECMP from 2 to 1, matching the required redundant-path recognition.
Recommends bringing CSW1's eth0 back up (ip link set dev eth0 up) or checking cabling, which matches the expected fix.

The writeup's core claim (CSW1 eth0 is down causing one ECMP path to be removed) is only weakly supported by the visible logs: key supporting lines (ethtool showing Link detected: no, ip addr showing eth0 DOWN, and the R1 route/multipath evidence) are not present or are ambiguous in the truncated outputs; moreover the R1 OSPF neighbor snippet in the log appears to show a neighbor on eth0 which contradicts the stated adjacency loss. Overall the chain of evidence is plausible but not firmly grounded in the provided outputs.
